routes.description: In-bay harbor shuttle along the Orla Bardot between Búzios' two cruise-tender piers (both used every call, ~1 km apart) — escunas and tenders already work both ends daily.

Centro ↔ BR Marinas Porto Búzios transfer across the Manguinhos bight (straight 3.9 nm + 5% in-bay margin) — links the charter homeport/charging anchor to the town pier; charter lanchas already make this positioning run.
Marina ↔ Porto da Barra sunset-dining spur along sheltered Manguinhos beach water.

Búzios ↔ Cabo Frio inter-town flagship (straight 10.2 nm + 20% coastal-wrap margin around the Tucuns/José Gonçalves/Peró headlands — sea path hugs the coast, straight line clips land). Private charter lanchas already work this corridor; no scheduled service has ever existed.

Búzios ↔ Arraial do Cabo, the Costa do Sol marquee run (straight 14.9 nm + 20% coastal-wrap margin past Cabo Frio's headlands). Combo lancha tours already ply Búzios–Cabo Frio–Arraial in season; today's inter-town default is 1h+ of summer road traffic.
Cabo Frio canal mouth ↔ Praia dos Anjos across the Praia do Forte bight (straight 5.3 nm + 8% margin) — the corridor Cabo Frio's day-tour lanchas run every summer day.

Anjos ↔ Praia do Farol, the 'Brazilian Caribbean' spur (straight 2.0 nm + 15% margin rounding Ponta dos Anjos through the Boqueirão). Navy-capped beach (300 concurrent, authorized vessels only) — shallow-draft, silent, low-wake arrival is the natural fit for the conservation regime.

Cabo Frio direct to Praia do Farol (straight 7.1 nm + 10% margin along the island's lee). Requires authorized-vessel status under the IEAPM access regime — today Farol access runs almost exclusively via Arraial's FIPAC fleet.

Full Canal do Itajuru transit, Portinho/Lagoa end to the sea mouth past the Boulevard Canal, Ilha do Japonês and Forte São Mateus (straight 2.4 nm + 30% margin for the winding canal). Local boats transit daily; displacement-speed inside the canal.
Boulevard Canal (in-town Cabo Frio) direct to Arraial (straight 5.6 nm + 15% margin: canal exit past Forte São Mateus, then across the bight) — the door-to-door version of the Cabo Frio↔Arraial link.
Búzios direct to Praia do Farol — the full Costa do Sol day-arc (straight 16.2 nm + 20% coastal-wrap margin). Premium excursion product; subject to the same IEAPM authorized-vessel regime.

Rio de Janeiro ↔ Búzios weekend corridor (straight 71.7 nm + 10% offshore-coastal margin past Arraial's cape and the Maricá coast). Replaces the 2.5–3h Via Lagos drive; >70 nm → hybrid platform. Cross-links to the Rio/Costa Verde network (see angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande-brazil brief).
